title: Cat and Mouse in Partnership
next_title: The Youth Who Learned to Shudder
source: Grimm, Household Tales, tr. Margaret Hunt (1884), tale 2
lesson: Watch who you share your pot with.
lines: Never let a cat babysit your butter. A Cat persuaded a Mouse to set up house together.
For winter, they bought a pot of fat and hid it under the church altar.
Soon the Cat said, My cousin's asked me to be godmother to her baby. Back tonight. She went straight to the church and licked the top off the fat.
What's the baby called? asked the Mouse. Top-Off.
A week later: another christening. Half the pot gone. This one's called Half-Done. Then a third. All-Gone. The Mouse shook her head.
Winter came. They went to the church. The pot was empty. Now I see! Top-Off, Half-Done… One more word and I'll eat you! …All-Gone!
And that was the end of the Mouse. Watch who you share your pot with.
Next time: a boy who has never been scared goes looking for fear. Follow so you don't miss it!
